page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.13xlarge is a compute-optimized instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 52 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz across 26 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It includes 96.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.85 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512, and AVX-512 VNNI are supported along with AES, BMI2, and FMA instructions. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, relying on network-attached block storage and offering a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Performance evaluation across benchmark suites places the multi-threaded capabilities of this instance within average ranges relative to market standards. The multi-core stress-ng score reaches 45505.98, and the Passmark CPU score is registered at 36916.67. Multi-threaded decompression tasks achieve 190.74 GB/sec using bzip3. However, single-core execution profiles rank lower, as shown by a single-core stress-ng score of 1311.39 and single-threaded gzip compression at 22.9 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory read bandwidth is recorded at 101.16 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 36.51 GB/sec.

The instance demonstrates solid throughput in parallel compute applications, achieving 40.39 million operations per second in Redis SET performance and a static web serving rate of 22.62 GB/sec. Given its low RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 1.85 GB per core and lack of local storage, the instance prioritizes CPU core density for distributed or stateless batch operations over memory-heavy in-memory databases. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, web serving clusters, parallel CI/CD build runners, and multi-threaded CPU computational tasks.

Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it features vector extensions including AVX-512 VNNI alongside cryptography and bit manipulation acceleration. The instance provides 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate moderate multi-core performance with a Geekbench multi-core score of 11386.0, Passmark CPU score of 36916.67, and 40.39 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core throughput remains in lower tiers. With 1.85 GB of RAM per vCPU, this configuration offers high parallel execution capacity tailored for stateless batch processing, software compilation, static web serving, and distributed CI/CD build environments.
